faults.failure: formal counterexample on CHK-003 (a_CHK_003, verif/sva/nnc_chk_alert.sv:97): No alert without an alert cause
faults.spec_says: spec/gpio_Design_Specification.md:1079-1081 [INT-INTG-002]: "When `i_a_intg_flip` is 1, bit 0 of `a_user.cmd_intg` is inverted. Line 963: "fatal_fault | This fatal alert is triggered when a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault is detected." Line 1164 D-017: "After a request with `i_a_intg_flip` = 1 is accepted, `o_alert` shall pulse no later than 16 cycles later...". This is an upper bound measured from acceptance; it does not say an alert must not appear before acceptance. Lines 1076-1077 [INT-INTG-001] (GP-4.2-01, the only rule cited by CHK-003): "A request with `i_a_intg_flip` = 0 therefore always carries correct integrity". The rule says nothing about when a request with intg_flip=1 may raise the alert. spec/opentitan_tlul_bus_specification.md:83 defines a_valid as "Request from host is valid", so a request exists once a_valid=1, not only at the handshake. Lines 1067-1068 [INT-TL-003]: the A-channel signals stay stable while a_valid=1 and a_ready=0, so a presented request is committed and must eventually be accepted. The contract text for CHK-003 (contract.json:366) narrows cause (a) to "an A handshake with i_a_intg_flip=1". That narrowing is the contract's own wording and is not in the spec.
faults.verification_does: verif/sva/nnc_chk_alert.sv:48 `a_hs = i_a_valid && o_a_ready`. Line 72 sets intg_seen_q only on `a_hs && i_a_intg_flip`. Line 82 `cause_a = intg_seen_q || (a_hs && i_a_intg_flip)`. So a flipped-integrity request counts as a cause only once it is accepted. Lines 50-51 and 83 give cause_b (ALERT_TEST write with data[0]=1, plus a 16-cycle window after its response). Line 97 asserts `o_alert |-> alert_cause`. Nothing in the checker covers a flipped request that is presented (i_a_valid=1) but still waiting for o_a_ready.
faults.what_to_change: B (recommended): extend cause (a) in contract CHK-003 and in nnc_chk_alert.sv so that a flipped-integrity request counts from the moment it is presented. Change line 72 to `if (i_a_valid && i_a_intg_flip) intg_seen_q <= 1'b1;` and line 82 to `cause_a = intg_seen_q || (i_a_valid && i_a_intg_flip);`, and change the contract wording from "an A handshake with i_a_intg_flip=1" to "a cycle with i_a_valid=1 and i_a_intg_flip=1". This follows spec:1079-1081 and 963 and keeps the property that traffic with i_a_intg_flip=0 never raises an alert. Other checkers that switch off from "an A handshake with i_a_intg_flip=1" (CHK-004/006/007/013) may need the same change; review them. C: ask the spec owner to state in D-017 / INT-INTG-002 whether the integrity fault exists, and may raise the alert, when a request with i_a_intg_flip=1 is presented (a_valid=1) or only when it is accepted. E: adding the TL-T3.1.3.4-02 mask-set assumption to nnc_env.sv is consistent with CHK-011(d), but it would not remove this counterexample. Do not add an assumption that forbids i_a_intg_flip=1 while o_a_ready=0, because the spec has no such host obligation.

changes.why: CHK-003 counted a request with i_a_intg_flip=1 as an alert cause only once it was accepted (A handshake). The spec does not say that. INT-INTG-002 says that a request with i_a_intg_flip=1 has a command integrity error, which is a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault that triggers fatal_fault. In TL-UL, a request exists as soon as a_valid=1. INT-TL-003 says a presented request stays stable until accepted. D-017 gives only an upper bound (16 cycles), measured from acceptance; it does not forbid an earlier alert. So the checker now records cause (a) in any cycle with i_a_valid=1 and i_a_intg_flip=1, both in the sticky intg_seen_q and in the same-cycle term. This makes the checker follow the spec without weakening anything the spec requires. Traffic with i_a_intg_flip=0 (INT-INTG-001) still never counts as a cause. Cause (b), CHK-001/002, the assertion, its counters and the CHK-003 reference are unchanged.
